_why: Gemma 4 26B-A4B has been installed since 17.08.2026 and had NEVER been
measured with this instrument - no bench/speed.py report existed for it on
04.09.2026, and setup/env/gemma26.env was written before this repo measured
anything. This file settles the two flags that profile cannot justify: the
backend, and the speculation.
WHY THE THIRD ARM IS GOOGLE'S OWN DRAFT MODEL, and why it is the reason this
file exists. google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant is a purpose-built 4-layer
drafter, 0.30 GiB at Q4_0, published for exactly this model. Verified
04.09.2026 out of the GGUF headers: general.architecture = gemma4-assistant,
nextn_predict_layers 4, token_embd.weight present, and embedding_length_out
2816 against the served model's gemma4.embedding_length 2816 - they match.
The string 'gemma4-assistant' is present in libllama.so of BOTH builds named
below, checked with strings rather than assumed from the source tree.
THE ROUTE IS -md <assistant> --spec-type draft-mtp AND IT IS NOT GUESSABLE
FROM THE FLAG NAME. --spec-type has no 'gemma4-assistant' value at all
(common/speculative.cpp lists eleven names and that is not one of them); the
assistant is driven by the draft-mtp implementation, which carries three
modes and picks the gemma one by is_mem_shared - true when the draft
context's ctx_other is the target context. If the wiring is WRONG the server
says so in as many words: 'Gemma4Assistant requires ctx_other to be set'
(src/llama-context.cpp:146). That line did not appear in any load on
AND THE ASSISTANT DOES NOT DOUBLE THE KV CACHE, which is the finding that
separates it from yesterday's model. Measured 04.09.2026 by two two-point
pairs (bench/reports/2026-09-04_1810_gemma26-memory): 21.97 KiB/token
without the drafter and 24.0 with it. GLM-4.7-Flash's MTP head measured 55.0
against 110.0 on the same machine the same day - EXACTLY double, because
that path allocates a second full-size KV cache. This one shares the
target's, so the drafter costs 0.56 GiB of base and ~2 KiB/token instead of
a second cache.
WHY THE ARMS ARE PARALLEL AND NOT CUMULATIVE, deliberately unlike
glm47flash.json. There the third arm was draft-mtp,ngram-mod so it could be
read against the ngram arm as 'what the head adds'. Here each speculation
arm carries exactly ONE drafter off the same floor, because the question is
which of the two drafters this profile should serve, not what they are worth
stacked. Combining them is a further question and gets its own run if either
wins.
base_args NAMES NO --spec-type AT ALL, and that is load-bearing rather than
tidy. --spec-type ACCUMULATES in llama.cpp (common/arg.cpp uses push_back),
so a control expressed as an override does not turn anything off - on
04.09.2026 two 'no-MTP control' loads came back byte-identical to the arms
they were controls for. A genuine control needs argv that never names the
flag, which is what the two nospec arms below are.
--spec-draft-p-min 0.75 IS IN BOTH SPECULATED ARMS AND IS NOT THE VARIABLE.
It is the house value, carried so the two drafters are compared on equal
terms. What p-min is worth on THIS model is a separate question and is
answered with bench/speed.py, not here - a sweep that varied it would be
comparing two things at once.
--spec-draft-n-max 4 matches the assistant's own nextn_predict_layers 4,
read out of its GGUF. Note the draft-mtp driver only clamps n_max to the
head count in its chain_heads mode, which is NOT the mode this model uses,
so the value is a real choice here rather than a formality.
NO --swa-full IN ANY CELL, AND NO --mmproj. --swa-full is a MEMORY axis on
this model and an expensive one - measured 04.09.2026 at 11x the KV per
token - but it changes what is ALLOCATED, not how far attention reads, so it
is not the backend's business and would only add GTT to six cells. The
profile's decision about it is taken from the memory report and from the
prompt-cache argument, not from here. --mmproj is left out for the reason
every sweep here leaves it out: clean text-only numbers.
THE BUILD DIRECTORIES ARE NAMED, NOT SYMLINKED. build-rocm-patched is a
symlink and what it points at changes; a recorded cell may not.
THE VULKAN ARM IS HANDICAPPED AND THE HANDICAP IS KNOWN, carried verbatim
from the qwen36 and glm47flash findings: build-vulkan is commit 54ee5ee of
22.08. against the ROCm arm's b10750-10, on a stack where a build difference
has been worth 25 %, and there is no RADV APU heap option set on this
machine at all. So a Vulkan LOSS here is weak evidence and a Vulkan WIN is
strong evidence. NOTE the profile has served build-vulkan since 17.08. on no
measurement whatsoever - that is what these six cells are for.
-c 65536 throughout, -np 1, f16 KV: clean single-stream numbers and the same
window in every cell. -np 1 is not a fresh decision - two independent
defects were measured on this hardware at two slots (the gfx1151 HIP race,
llama.cpp #27579, and slot-restore poisoning; the matrix is in
setup/env/qwen38.env). f16 KV rather than the q8_0 the profile carried until
04.09.2026: this repo's objection to q8 KV is a CORRECTNESS objection, not a
speed one - it dropped qwen38's long-context task.
THE PORT IS 8080 AND IT IS NOT A FREE CHOICE. bench/sweep.py polls /slots
there and stops production for the duration, so 8080 is free and there is
nothing to sit beside. 8081 cost six cells and twenty-five minutes on
04.09.2026, and the failure text - 'model loaded, but /slots never answered'
- accuses the server while the server answers curl in 0.7 ms. Now tested
across every variants file against SWEEP.URL.
@MODELS@ and @HOME@ are expanded by setup/lib/systemdfile.py - never an
absolute path, which would tie this file to one checkout.

variants.name: rocm-nospec
variants.note: The floor: no drafter of any kind, and a genuine control because base_args never names --spec-type. Every other cell is read against this one. The build is the pin the other profiles serve MTP from, not the house build.

variants.name: vulkan-nospec
variants.note: The backend, alone, and the cell that decides whether the profile's LLAMA_BIN was ever right. It has flipped before: Vulkan won for laguna without speculation, ROCm won 2x for qwen38 with it, qwen36 SPLIT, and glm47flash did not split at all. Expect no fixed pattern.

variants.name: rocm-ngram
variants.note: The drafter that needs no second model, drafting from the PROMPT. Read the COPY workload and not just count: this repo once recorded 'the ngram drafters give nothing' from a probe that could not have shown one working (bench/README.md). High acceptance on NOVEL prose means the opposite of good news - it means the model is repeating the prompt.

variants.name: vulkan-ngram
variants.note: The fourth corner. Not decoration: without it, a backend that wins without speculation and loses with it would look like a single verdict - which is exactly what qwen36 did.

variants.name: rocm-assistant
variants.note: Google's own drafter, on the pinned ROCm build. This is the lever the whole exercise is about, and the one that decided qwen36's day at 0.3 GiB instead of 17. Read draft_accept_pct AND tg_tps together: on glm47flash the head accepted 59-82 % of its drafts and cost up to 42 % of throughput, so acceptance is not a speed prediction.

variants.name: vulkan-assistant
variants.note: The same drafter on the build the profile actually serves. The one most likely to fail outright rather than lose: build-vulkan is two weeks older than the ROCm arm. A failure here is a fact about that build and has to be reported as one, not as a fact about the backend. NOTE the memory pairs of 04.09.2026 were all taken on THIS build and the drafter loaded correctly there.
